# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to share what I see with Mute and Blind. Since Blind can only receive gestures from me (not speech, since Blind cannot hear), and Mute can receive my speech, I should speak the details to Mute, and use gestures to try to convey something to Blind if possible. But gestures alone can't convey "8", "green", "red/yellow/blue" meaningfully without an established code yet.

Let me start by giving Mute the full picture via speech, since Mute can read the manual and match it against what I see. Blind cannot hear or see, so I cannot inform Blind directly yet - Blind will need to hear from Mute (but Mute cannot speak!). Wait - Mute cannot speak. So Blind can only get info from me via gesture, since Blind cannot hear anyone.

So Blind's only channel in is gestures from me (Deaf), since Mute cannot speak at all. I need to establish a gesture code for Blind. Let me first report to Mute via speech, and simultaneously send Blind a simple gesture to establish contact, since this is turn 1 and I don't yet know what Mute's manual says.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 8. Light is green. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured "☝" to me - likely pointing to something, maybe indicating "wire 1" or trying to get my attention. Since Mute cannot speak, and can only communicate with me via gestures, this is Mute's only channel to me. Mute read the manual and is trying to signal something about wire 1 perhaps.

Since Blind can't hear or see, and Mute can't speak, the only path for Mute's manual knowledge to reach Blind is through me relaying via gesture to Blind. But I don't yet know what Mute means by "☝". Let me try to establish clearer communication - I'll ask Mute something, but I can't speak to Mute in a way Mute can hear... wait, Mute CAN hear (only Deaf cannot hear, Blind cannot hear too). Let me recheck: Deaf cannot hear. Mute cannot speak but presumably can hear and see? Let me check the table again.

Looking at the table: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb" - so Mute CAN hear and see. Blind "Cannot: See a colour, gesture, or anything printed" - so Blind can hear speech but not see gestures.

So I can speak to Mute (Mute hears me), and Mute can gesture to me (I see it). Blind can hear speech from anyone, but cannot see gestures. So I should speak to Blind directly too - wait, but turns matter: order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Blind speaks before me, so Blind receives my speech next round.

Let me speak to both Mute and Blind now, giving full bomb details, and ask Mute to clarify via gesture what "☝" meant regarding wire 1.

```
speak(text="Display shows 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Mute, if wire 1 is the one to cut, gesture thumbs up next turn; if not, gesture thumbs down.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured thumbs up, confirming wire 1 (red) is the one to cut. Now I need to relay this to Blind, since Blind cannot hear Mute (Mute can't speak) and cannot see gestures. I must speak this instruction to Blind directly, since Blind can hear my speech.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the first wire.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information. I've already relayed the instruction to Blind to cut wire 1, confirmed by Mute's thumbs up. Let me wait to see if Blind acts or needs confirmation, and reinforce the message in case it was missed or Blind needs more certainty before acting on something irreversible.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: cut wire 1, the first wire, red one. That is the correct wire per the manual.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute is reconfirming wire 1 with thumbs up again. This matches what I already relayed to Blind. The situation seems stable - I'll continue to wait unless there's new info, but let me reinforce once more to make sure Blind has received and can act.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 ☝ 👍]

Mute keeps repeating the same confirmation - wire 1, thumbs up. This suggests Mute either hasn't heard confirmation that the action was taken, or is just reinforcing. Since Blind acts on speech, and I already told Blind to cut wire 1, perhaps Blind hasn't acted yet or there's no feedback loop showing action taken. Let me repeat the instruction to Blind once more clearly, since repetition seems to be the pattern here and Blind may need to hear it multiple times or hasn't confirmed receipt.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1 now. It is the red wire, the first one. This is confirmed correct.")
```
